chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Jam sessions in town and sitting in with local bands on leave
summary: On leave he played in clubs at free jam sessions, such as ad lib versions of Stardust, and sat in with bands lacking a pianist.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But they all loved me and I loved them as men, and because I had this connection of helping them in that way, and I also played the piano in the mess hall. And then when I would go into town I'd play in these night clubs because at that time they had the famous jam sessions, j-a-m s-e-s-s-i-o-n which are now called jazz concerts.

But the difference was that in those days they allowed you to do this, the musician's union allowed you to do this free, and different musicians who liked to play, and there were a few who could play, they would go around and get together with other musicians who wanted to play
and expressed themselves with ad lib music, because of their knowledge of the chord progressions, you see.

In other words we would take pieces like Star Dust that was written by Hogie Carmichael, and very famous, and we would play the melody just long enough for you to know that we were playing 'Star Dust', and then we would start playing our ad lib versions and rhythmic conceptions of this piece. In our way these were known as jam sessions, like jam, you know, j-a-m.
Now they call them jazz concerts, right?
Okay. And they get paid a lot of money for it.
They get paid so much money for it it's not even funny, you know, the money that they get paid today I could have probably built a mansion with when I was coming up.

That's good, it shows that time moves on. But getting back to the story of that period, I would also be heard playing the piano in these different places, where people were having parties, and just like I played the house rent parties, many times in a night club they would always have a piano but no musicians.
Because first of all there wouldn't be any musicians around in the town available. All of the best musicians would be in the larger cities playing with bands which were touring the country.

Not only that, but in the process I would sit in with these bands, some of them. Some of them may not have a good piano player, or a piano player who was capable of playing solo, or didn't have the personality, or maybe he got sick or something, or maybe he didn't get paid or he didn't show up because he didn't have any money to get to the job. And I would play in their place.
So I was constantly heard by the guys in the army, in CC Camp, and that brought about this warmness between myself and these men in the army.
